summary: The Lennard-Jones force kernel takes 92% of samples. Its inner loop is scalar and dominated by the pair-distance cutoff test, so it is compute-bound on scalar floating point. Redistribution and link-cell sorting are a distant second.

supporting_evidence: 91.75% of 83K task-clock samples are in ljForce (perf-report.txt).
The annotated inner loop uses only scalar SSE instructions (vmulsd/vaddsd), with no packed FP (annotate/ljForce.txt).
Time per atom stays flat from 4K to 864K atoms (1.14 to 1.31 us/atom/task), so the loop is not cache-bound.
findings.likely_cause: Data-dependent continue statements for the cutoff and box-boundary checks, and possible aliasing of the force arrays, stop GCC from vectorizing the j-loop.
findings.experiment: Profiled lattice sizes 10, 20 and 40 with scripts/profile_target.sh --cmd to test cache sensitivity.
findings.experiment_result: Per-atom cost changed by less than 15% across a 200x change in footprint, which rules out a memory-bound loop and supports the compute-bound diagnosis.

supporting_evidence: 1.21% self time, plus msort_with_tmp in libc, called from redistributeAtoms every step (perf-report.txt).
findings.likely_cause: Halo cells are re-sorted with qsort on every step, although atoms move little between steps.
findings.experiment: None beyond the baseline; the cost is small enough that the source and call graph settle it.
findings.experiment_result: Not tested separately; the estimate comes from the baseline profile only.

limitations: No hardware PMU events in this VM: IPC, cache and branch misses could not be measured.
Only the serial build with the Lennard-Jones potential was profiled.
